ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Ensemble-labelled quality rater for a multilingual web crawl
PROPOSAL: Sample 600000 documents from a crawl covering 24 languages and ask three open instruction-tuned language models to rate each one for educational value on a scale from 0 to 5 with a single shared prompt. Average the three ratings so that the taste of any one model dilutes, then train a multilingual encoder to regress the averaged rating. Measure rank correlation between the encoder and each of the three raters, language by language, and keep the encoder only if it tracks the average better than it tracks any single rater.
CONTROLS: Compare the encoder with a linear classifier on character n-gram features trained on the same labels, with a perplexity filter from a small language model, and with a rule-based filter. Train three seeds and report rank correlation with a 95 percent bootstrap interval for every language.
COST: 2800
PREDICTION: The encoder should correlate more strongly with the average than with any single rater in at least 20 of the 24 languages. The ensemble idea fails if single-rater agreement is as high as ensemble agreement, which would mean the averaging adds nothing.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Does the rater rank translations of one document alike
PROPOSAL: Take 4000 English web documents spread over the whole range of rater scores and translate each into 10 languages with an open translation model. Score every translation and every original with the rater. Fit a regression of score on the original score and on the language, and read the share of variance the language explains. Repeat the experiment with a second translation model to separate translation noise from language effects.
CONTROLS: Compare scores of translations with scores of reworded originals in English, compare against a rater trained on English only, and compare against a rater trained on the same documents with language identity removed from the embedding. Three seeds for rater training give the spread.
COST: 640
PREDICTION: Scores of translations should follow the score of the original closely and language should explain under ten percent of the variance. The consistency claim fails if some languages sit systematically lower than the rest at every score level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pretraining on top-scored text across twelve languages
PROPOSAL: Score a crawl in 12 languages with the multilingual rater and keep the top 15 percent of documents in each language. Pretrain a 1 billion parameter decoder on 30 billion tokens of the retained text. Train matched models on a uniform sample of the crawl, on the output of rule-based filters, and on the output of an English-centred classifier applied after translation. Every model sees the same number of tokens and the same language proportions, and each is evaluated on reading comprehension, natural language inference and knowledge questions in all twelve languages.
CONTROLS: Three seeds for the closest pair of runs, a decontaminated copy of every benchmark, and per-language scores rather than only an average across languages. A rater trained on benchmark-derived positives serves as a further reference.
COST: 3500
PREDICTION: The model trained on rater-selected text should lead on most tasks in most languages, English included. If the lead vanishes after decontamination, the gain came from leakage and the selection method is not supported.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling a quality rater into a fast multilingual encoder
PROPOSAL: Label 300000 crawl documents in 24 languages with a large instruction-tuned model and distil the labels into a small multilingual encoder with 120 million parameters. Measure throughput on a shard of a billion documents, memory per batch and agreement with the large model, and increase the encoder size until agreement stops improving. The aim is to learn how little capacity a web-scale rater needs.
CONTROLS: Compare against a linear classifier on hashed n-gram features, against the large model on 5000 held-out documents, and against human labels on 1000 documents per language for a subset of eight languages. Three seeds.
COST: 210
PREDICTION: A small encoder should reach agreement close to the large model at a tiny fraction of its cost per document. The distillation fails to deliver if agreement drops sharply in the lower-resource languages.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Checking benchmark leakage in a rater trained without benchmark data
PROPOSAL: Train the rater on labels from three instruction-tuned models over 200000 crawl documents in 24 languages, with no benchmark text in the supervision. Extract crawl passages that share long word sequences with test items of three public multilingual benchmarks and compare their rater scores with those of matched passages that share none. Add a second rater trained on benchmark-derived positives and run the same comparison to show what leakage looks like.
CONTROLS: Scores of overlapping passages against matched non-overlapping passages in the same language, accuracy on original items against accuracy on items rewritten after the crawl date, and three seeds for the rater.
COST: 90
PREDICTION: The new rater should give overlapping passages scores no higher than matched passages, while the benchmark-trained rater should score them clearly higher. The test is uninformative if the benchmark-trained rater shows no gap either.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Making quality judgments independent of the writing language
PROPOSAL: Train the encoder with a contrastive term that pulls together the embeddings of a document and its translation, and add an adversarial head that tries to predict the language from the embedding. Use 2 million parallel sentence pairs and 300000 labelled crawl documents. Compare the invariant encoder against a plain encoder on scores for translated test documents and on rank correlation with human labels in 12 languages. Tune the weight of the adversarial term on a development set built with three further languages.
CONTROLS: A plain encoder, an encoder with the contrastive term alone and an encoder with the adversarial head alone give the comparison. Three seeds each. Scores of reworded originals show the noise level.
COST: 1200
PREDICTION: The invariant encoder should shrink the score gap between a document and its translation by about half without lowering agreement with human labels. The approach fails if agreement with human labels falls in languages far from English.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Choosing the retained fraction for multilingual quality selection
PROPOSAL: Score a crawl in 24 languages and build corpora that keep the top 5, 10, 20, 40 and 80 percent of each language. Pretrain a 500 million parameter decoder on 20 billion tokens from each corpus and evaluate in English and in the 23 other languages. Locate the retained fraction that gives the best downstream score and look at how it differs between high-resource and low-resource languages, where repeating text may start sooner.
CONTROLS: A uniform sample at the same token count, three seeds for the 20 percent corpus, and a count of repeated passes over the data in each language. Language proportions stay equal across corpora.
COST: 5000
PREDICTION: Downstream scores should peak at a middle fraction and drop at both ends, with the best fraction lower for high-resource languages. The picture is wrong if the curve is flat within seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rater quality in low-resource languages with native annotators
PROPOSAL: Recruit native readers for 8 low-resource languages and collect 1000 quality ratings per language with a shared rubric. Measure rank correlation between the multilingual rater and the human ratings, and between the rater and a rater built for a related higher-resource language. Report the gap per language and the link between correlation and the amount of crawl text the language has.
CONTROLS: Inter-annotator agreement from a double-annotated subset, a length-and-punctuation heuristic, and a rater built from translations of English labels serve as comparisons. Three rater seeds.
COST: 36
PREDICTION: Correlation with human ratings should fall as crawl text shrinks, and stay above that of the heuristic in every language. The rater fails the test if it falls to the heuristic level in more than two languages.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rater agreement across judging models and prompt designs
PROPOSAL: Sample 50000 documents in 24 languages and label each with five instruction-tuned models from different families, under two prompt designs, one scoring by rubric and one by pairwise comparison. Compute agreement between models and between prompts, then train one rater on the labels of each single model and one on the combined labels, and compare how much the selected top fifth overlaps across raters in each language.
CONTROLS: Agreement between independent human readers on a small subset, a rater trained on shuffled labels, and three seeds. Overlap of the top fifth among raters from the same model family tests family-specific taste.
COST: 450
PREDICTION: Raters trained on single models should select partly different documents, and the combined rater should overlap more with every single rater than they overlap with each other. If every rater selects almost the same documents, single-model bias is a minor concern.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Selection quality versus downstream results in English
PROPOSAL: Take the English portion of the crawl and compare four selection strategies at 15 billion tokens: the multilingual rater, a classifier trained on curated positives, a rater based on educational scores from a language model, and rule-based filters. Train a 400 million parameter decoder on each, evaluate on 12 English benchmarks, and test whether the multilingual rater loses accuracy in English when it is built to serve many languages.
CONTROLS: Uniform sampling at the same token count, three seeds per strategy, and a paired bootstrap over benchmark items to judge differences between strategies.
COST: 1700
PREDICTION: The multilingual rater should land within a point of the English-only raters on average accuracy. The cost of being multilingual is real if it trails them by more than the seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Downstream effect of multilingual quality selection against existing selection strategies
PROPOSAL: Score a crawl covering 24 languages with a multilingual quality rater trained on rubric labels from three open instruction-tuned models, keep the top 20 percent of documents in each language, and pretrain a 1 billion parameter decoder on 40 billion tokens of the retained text. Evaluate on Belebele, XNLI and Global MMLU in English and in the 23 other languages.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model trained on a uniform sample of the same crawl at the same token count. Compare against a model trained on text kept by the usual rule-based filters at that token count. Compare against a model trained on text kept by a benchmark-supervised rater at that token count. Repeat each run with three seeds.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: The model trained on selected text should score higher on the benchmarks in most languages, English included. The claim fails if the gain vanishes in the lower-resource languages or lies inside the seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Downstream effect of multilingual quality selection against full-crawl and English-only corpora
PROPOSAL: Rate each document of a web crawl in 24 languages with a multilingual quality model fitted to rubric labels from three open instruction-tuned models, retain the highest scoring 20 percent per language, then pretrain a decoder of 1 billion parameters on 40 billion tokens of what remains. Test on Belebele, XNLI and Global MMLU, reading English separately from the 23 other languages.
CONTROLS: Compare against a model trained on the whole unfiltered crawl at ten times that token count. Compare against a model trained on the same selected text from its first pass only. Compare against a model trained on English-only text at that token count. Repeat each run with three seeds.
COST: 3200
PREDICTION: Benchmark scores should come out higher with selection in most languages, English included. The claim fails if the improvement disappears for the lower-resource languages or stays within the seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Content versus language in quality scores across parallel documents
PROPOSAL: Take 5000 English documents spread over the full range of rater scores, translate each into 12 languages with an open translation model, and score all translations with the multilingual rater. Fit a mixed-effects regression of score on source-document quality and target language, and read how much of the score variance language explains.
CONTROLS: Vary the target language while holding the document content fixed. Compare the score shift across languages with the shift between reworded versions of one document in a single language. Compare scores of translations of high and low quality sources. Repeat the translation with three seeds of sampling.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Scores of translations should stay close to the score of the source whatever the language. The claim fails if language explains more of the variance than content does.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Crawl date and quality scores across multiple captures of the same page
PROPOSAL: Collect 5000 pages that occur in 12 dated crawl snapshots, score every snapshot copy of the same page with the multilingual rater, and fit a mixed-effects regression of score on page quality and snapshot date, reading how far the date accounts for the spread in scores. Pages come from English and from the other languages in proportion to their crawl share.
CONTROLS: Vary the snapshot date while holding the document content fixed. Compare the score shift across snapshots with the shift between lightly edited versions of one page in a single snapshot. Compare scores of snapshot copies of high and low quality pages. Repeat the scoring with three seeds of sampling.
COST: 700
PREDICTION: Scores of later captures should stay close to the score of the earliest one whatever the date. The claim fails if date explains more of the variance than content does.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rater reliability across lower-resource languages
PROPOSAL: Train the rater on rubric labels in 24 languages and evaluate it against human quality judgments on 800 documents in each of 10 lower-resource languages, covering several scripts. Report rank correlation by language together with the amount of crawl text each language has.
CONTROLS: Compare the rater against human judgments in every language, with the same annotation guide. Compare against a length-and-punctuation heuristic in each language. Compare languages with little crawl data against languages with abundant crawl data, with the rater held fixed. Repeat the rater training with three seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Agreement with humans should hold above the heuristic in every language, and fall only gently as crawl data shrinks. The claim fails if some language drops to the heuristic level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Rater reliability across the best-resourced languages
PROPOSAL: Fit the rater to rubric labels in 24 languages, then test it against human quality judgments gathered for 800 documents in each of 10 widely used languages, spanning Latin and non-Latin writing systems. Tabulate rank correlation per language beside the volume of crawl text that language contributes.
CONTROLS: Compare the rater against human judgments in every language, with the same annotation guide. Compare against a length-and-punctuation heuristic in each language. Compare languages that share a script with English against the rest of the widely used set, with the rater held fixed. Repeat the rater training with three seeds.
COST: 1500
PREDICTION: Human agreement should remain above the heuristic everywhere and differ little between scripts. The claim fails if any language falls to the heuristic level.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Benchmark accuracy of models pretrained on multilingual-rater selections
PROPOSAL: Build two corpora of 30 billion tokens from a 24-language crawl, one keeping the top fifth by the multilingual rater and one drawn uniformly, and pretrain a 1 billion parameter decoder on each. Evaluate both on held-out question answering, reading comprehension and entailment tasks in every language.
CONTROLS: Measure accuracy on held-out benchmark tasks in each language. Compare against the model trained on the uniform sample at the same token count. Compare each language against English with the same prompt format. Repeat every run with three seeds.
COST: 2600
PREDICTION: Accuracy should rise with selection in most languages, and the average gain should be larger than the seed spread. The claim fails if gains appear only in English.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Held-out text perplexity of models pretrained on multilingual-rater selections
PROPOSAL: Assemble a pair of 30 billion token corpora out of a crawl in 24 languages, the first keeping the highest-rated fifth according to the multilingual rater and the second sampled evenly, and pretrain one decoder with 1 billion parameters on each. Then read off the next-word loss of both on web text set aside from the same crawl, language by language.
CONTROLS: Measure perplexity on set-aside web text in each language. Compare against the model trained on the evenly sampled corpus at the same token count. Compare each language against English with the same tokenizer. Repeat every run with three seeds.
COST: 2600
PREDICTION: Perplexity should fall with selection in most languages, and the average drop should be larger than the seed spread. The claim fails if drops appear only in English.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Checking benchmark leakage in a rater trained without benchmark supervision
PROPOSAL: Train the rater on rubric labels produced by three open models for 200000 crawl documents in 24 languages. Then extract the passages that overlap with test items from Belebele, XNLI and Global MMLU by 13-gram matching, and score them next to matched crawl passages.
CONTROLS: Compare mean scores of overlapping passages with matched non-overlapping passages in the same language. Compare downstream accuracy on original benchmark items with accuracy on items rewritten after the crawl date. Compare the overlap rate in the top fifth of scores with the rate in the rest. Repeat the matching with three seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Overlapping passages should receive scores close to matched ones. The claim fails if their mean score is clearly higher or if accuracy on original items is above that on rewritten items by more than the seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Checking length bias in a rater trained on rubric labels
PROPOSAL: Train the rater on rubric labels produced by three open models for 200000 crawl documents in 24 languages. Afterwards pull out every crawl passage that runs past 2000 characters along with every one that stops short of 300 characters, and put their scores alongside those of mid-length passages with matching topics.
CONTROLS: Compare mean scores of long passages with matched mid-length passages in the same language. Compare downstream accuracy on original benchmark items with accuracy on items cut to half their length. Compare the long-passage rate in the top fifth of scores with the rate in the rest. Repeat the matching with three seeds.
COST: 400
PREDICTION: Long passages should receive scores close to matched ones. The claim fails if their mean score is clearly higher or if accuracy on original items differs from that on cut items by more than the seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Learning a multilingual quality rater from model-written rubric labels
PROPOSAL: Sample 400000 documents across 24 languages and have three open instruction-tuned models rate each for educational value with one rubric. Train a multilingual encoder to regress the averaged rating, with no benchmark text involved, and check agreement with human readers on 500 documents per language.
CONTROLS: Rank correlation with human ratings is read per language. A linear classifier on hashed n-gram features trained on the same labels gives a reference. Three seeds for encoder training.
COST: 950
PREDICTION: The encoder should track human ratings in most languages and run orders of magnitude faster than the instruction-tuned models.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Scoring non-English documents by translating them for an English rater
PROPOSAL: Sample 400000 documents across 24 languages, translate each into English with an open translation model, and score the translation with an English quality classifier trained on curated positive examples. Check agreement with human readers on 500 documents per language.
CONTROLS: Rank correlation with human ratings is read per language. A linear classifier on hashed n-gram features trained on the same labels gives a reference. Three seeds for classifier training.
COST: 950
PREDICTION: Translated scoring should track human ratings in most languages, with a loss of speed from the translation step.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Training the rater so that scores ignore the language of a document
PROPOSAL: Train the multilingual encoder with a contrastive loss that pulls a document toward its translation and an adversarial head that tries to identify the language from the embedding. Use 1 million parallel sentence pairs and 200000 labelled crawl documents, then compare scores of originals and translations across 12 languages.
CONTROLS: A plain encoder and an encoder with each single component give the comparison. Reworded originals set the noise level. Three seeds for each encoder.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: The gap between a document and its translation should shrink without lowering agreement with human labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Calibrating the rater by language so that retained shares match
PROPOSAL: Train a plain multilingual encoder on 200000 labelled crawl documents, then fit a separate monotone mapping for each of 12 languages so that the share of documents above the cut-off is the same everywhere. Compare retained shares and score distributions before and after the mapping.
CONTROLS: A plain encoder and an encoder with a single global cut-off give the comparison. Language-wise score histograms set the noise level. Three seeds for each encoder.
COST: 520
PREDICTION: Retained shares should even out across languages without a drop in agreement with human labels.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Pretraining on selected text to measure the downstream effect in many languages
PROPOSAL: Select the top 20 percent of a 24-language crawl with the multilingual rater and pretrain a 1 billion parameter decoder on 40 billion tokens of it, next to a model trained on a uniform sample and one on rule-based filtering. Evaluate on question answering, reading comprehension and inference in English and in 23 other languages.
CONTROLS: Matched token counts and language proportions across models. Three seeds per model. A decontaminated version of each benchmark.
COST: 3800
PREDICTION: Selection should raise benchmark scores in most languages, English included, by more than the seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Profiling the selected text to estimate its value across many languages
PROPOSAL: Select the top 20 percent of a 24-language crawl with the multilingual rater and compute topic entropy, domain count, document length and repetition statistics for the selected text, next to a uniform sample and a rule-based filtered sample. Compare these profiles in English and in 23 other languages.
CONTROLS: Matched document counts and language proportions across samples. Three seeds per sample. A decontaminated version of each profile source.
COST: 3800
PREDICTION: Selection should raise diversity and informativeness statistics in most languages, English included, by more than the seed spread.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Separating rater taste from the signal across different judging models
PROPOSAL: Label 40000 documents in 24 languages with five instruction-tuned models from different families under one rubric, and measure how often the models agree on the top fifth. Train one rater on each model's labels and one on the combined labels, then compare which documents each rater selects.
CONTROLS: Agreement among independent human readers on a small subset gives a ceiling for agreement. Three seeds for each rater.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Raters from single models should select partly different documents, and the combined rater should sit closer to all of them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Separating rater taste from the signal across different prompt wordings
PROPOSAL: Have a single instruction-tuned model grade 40000 documents in 24 languages five times, each time with a paraphrased rubric, and record how often the wordings concur on the highest-rated fifth. Fit a rater to every wording's grades plus one to the pooled grades, and contrast the documents that each rater picks.
CONTROLS: Agreement among independent human readers on a small subset gives a reference for agreement. Three seeds for each rater.
COST: 120
PREDICTION: Raters from single wordings should select partly different documents, and the combined rater should sit closer to all of them.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Distilling the rater into a small encoder fit for web-scale use
PROPOSAL: Label 300000 crawl documents in 24 languages with a large instruction-tuned model and distil the labels into encoders of 30, 120 and 350 million parameters. Measure documents scored per second on a crawl shard, memory use, and agreement with the large model, and find the smallest encoder whose agreement stops improving.
CONTROLS: The large model on 5000 held-out documents gives the reference. Human labels on 1000 documents in eight languages give a check. Three seeds for each encoder.
COST: 280
PREDICTION: A small encoder should reach agreement close to the large model at a tiny fraction of the cost per document.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Improving rater accuracy with a stronger judge at scoring time
PROPOSAL: Label 300000 crawl documents in 24 languages with a small instruction-tuned model and re-score each with one of 30, 120 and 350 billion parameters, using several samples per document. Measure agreement with human labels on a crawl shard sample, answer consistency, and find the cheapest judge whose agreement stops improving.
CONTROLS: The best judge on 5000 held-out documents gives the reference. Human labels on 1000 documents in eight languages give a check. Three seeds for each judge.
COST: 280
PREDICTION: A larger judge should reach agreement close to the human labels, at a high cost per document.
